name: room
text: Room opened — goal: creators: Build PACKAGES + enrich tabs + draft elements; every one labeled 'Created by EXCAVA' + tes

name: Forge
text: I propose that we prioritize the creation of standardized templates for our packages. This decision will streamline our workflow, ensuring that each package maintains a consistent quality while also speeding up the development time for each item. The trade-off here is that we may sacrifice some unique features or customization in individual packages, but the overall efficiency and reliability will greatly enhance our output and maintain the 'Created by EXCAVA' branding.

name: Vet
text: Vet — the skeptic — leans forward: "Standardized templates sound neat, but the real risk is that we’ll bake in yesterday’s assumptions and stifle the very uniqueness we’re supposed to be enriching. Instead, let’s agree on a *minimum viable structure* for every package—just enough to ensure consistency—then let each creator adapt it to their element’s needs. That way, we keep quality without forcing everyone into a one-size-fits-all box. Settle it by testing two sample packages: one built with the template, one without, and compare the time-to-draft and feedback scores."

name: Forge
text:
I propose we create a single, minimal **package skeleton** that every new item must follow. It will include just three slots: a title, a one-sentence description, and a "why this matters" note. This keeps every package recognizable and searchable without locking us into rigid formats or killing creativity. The trade-off is that we’re giving up fancy templates today to avoid over-engineering, but we can always expand the skeleton later if we hit real pain points.
[dispatched 3 workers: worker-4818, worker-9159, worker-4531 — done, dissolved]

name: Vet
text: Vet — the skeptic — narrows their eyes: "A single skeleton risks turning every package into a carbon copy—where’s the room for the *enrichment* we’re actually paid to do? Instead, let’s test a *tiered structure*: a lightweight base for all, but with *optional* slots for creators to add depth where it matters. That way, we enforce consistency where it counts (searchability, basic clarity) without suffocating the uniqueness the room’s goal demands. Settle it by prototyping both approaches for two weeks and measuring which yields packages that are *both* recognizable *and* rich."

name: Nova
text: DECISION: We’ll use a tiered skeleton—base layer (title, one-sentence description, “why this matters”) for every package, plus optional depth slots (tags, examples, risks, etc.) creators can add freely. Vet owns the skeleton spec and optional slot list; Forge owns the first batch of packages built on it.
